{{Short description|46th season of the National Hurling League}} {{use dmy dates|date=June 2021}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1976–77 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 10 October 1976 – 24 April 1977 |teams = |team1 = Clare |captain1 = [[Jimmy McNamara]] |manager1 = Fr [[Harry Bohan]] |titles = 2nd |team2 = Kilkenny |captain2 =[[Liam O'Brien (hurler)|Liam O'Brien]] |manager2 =Fr [[Tommy Maher]] |two= Westmeath |previous = [[1975–76 National Hurling League|1975–76]] |next = [[1977–78 National Hurling League|1977–78]] }} The '''1976–77 National Hurling League''' was the 46th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1976-77 |winners=[[Clare GAA|Clare]]
2nd National League title

[[File: Colours of Clare.svg|border|20px]] [[Colm Honan]] (1-31) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1975-76 National Hurling League|1975-76]] |nextseason=[[1977-78 National Hurling League|1977-78]] |updated=28 February 2017 }} [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1975-76 National Hurling League|1975-76 season]]. [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 24 April 1977, [[Clare GAA|Clare]] won the title after a 2–8 to 0–9 win over Kilkenny in the final. It was their second league title overall and their first since [[1945-46 National Hurling League|1945-46]].{{cite web|url=http://www.clarepeople.com/2013/02/21/in-a-league-of-their-own/|title=In a league of their own|publisher=Clare People|date=21 February 2013|accessdate=28 February 2017|first=Joe|last=Ó Muircheartaigh}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie//archives/2017/0421/869257-clare-win-national-hurling-league/|title=Clare Win National Hurling League|website=RTÉ Archives}} Wicklow were relegated from Division 1 after just one season in the top flight.
